clue.text: Internal disorder with military officer left in charge

parts.note: CO is the commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer left in charge of a unit that is suffering some internal disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, a disorder of the insides, especially in babies and horses.

clue.text: Blood and punishment the reward for sportsmen?

parts.note: claret is old slang for blood, from its red colour
jug is slang for prison, so a spell of punishment

explanation.surface: Blood and punishment, grimly offered as what sportsmen earn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Claret Jug is the trophy awarded to the winner of the Open Championship in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf Open's trophy is a prize won by a sportsman, hence the question mark for a specific example.

clue.text: Discoloured Roman numerals

definitions.meaning: bruised a bluish-grey colour, as skin is
the string ... is made entirely of Roman numerals (50, 1, 5, 1, 500)

explanation.surface: Faded or stained numbers on a Roman monument.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid originally means bruise-coloured, bluish-grey, so a discoloured patch of skin.

clue.text: Match prisoner to previous record

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Police try to match a prisoner to a previous criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to correspond or agree with something, a verb meaning to match.

clue.text: Turn up without paying, being upset at charges

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of at charges are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arrives without paying, annoyed by the entry charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend an event uninvited, getting in without a ticket.

clue.text: Greed instinctive to US city, keeping Liberal enthralled

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the first parts hold the next piece
enthralled literally means held captive, so the abbreviation for Liberal is held within the rest

parts.note: a gut reaction is an instinctive one
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Greed comes naturally to an American city that keeps its Liberals spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' and 'enthralled' both say the Liberal abbreviation is held within the instinct word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is excessive greed, especially for food, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Top performers not needing second time in City

indicators.note: not needing means dropping, and second points to the later of the two T's in the phrase

parts.note: the very best performers are the best

explanation.surface: Star performers don't need a second chance in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BEST has two T's; only the second goes, leaving THEBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes is an ancient city, both in Egypt and in Greece.

clue.text: Puritan, no good in religious group, becomes criminal

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the sect

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

indicators.note: no here means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous, puritanical person

explanation.surface: A Puritan who has gone to the bad in a sect turns criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puritan' is not the religious group: it means a prig, a prudish moraliser.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of an offence, the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Ornamental number missing article at top

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so something is removed
at top says the removal is from the beginning of this down entry

parts.note: an anaesthetic is something that numbs, a number
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A decorative musical number lacking an article at the top of the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, pronounced NUM-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic means concerned with beauty, so it describes something decorative or pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Reckless bears, totally without heart

parts.note: to bear something is to have it

indicators.note: without heart means the middle letters are removed, keeping only the outside ones

explanation.surface: Bears are heartless and reckless in their behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means acting too quickly, without due thought, so rash or reckless.

clue.text: Now certain to miss special experience

parts.note: Advent is the season before Christmas, the current season when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: to miss means to go without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Something certain to miss out on a special experience at this time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now' is topical: the puzzle appeared in December, so the present season is Advent.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an unusual and exciting experience or undertaking.

clue.text: More than one pedal shape is durable

definitions.meaning: foot-shaped blocks on which shoes are made, pedal meaning of the foot
something that endures continues to hold up

explanation.surface: A cyclist observes that pedals of one shape hold up well.
explanation.definitionFit: A last is a cobbler's foot model; and to last means to endure.

clue.text: Last demons ruined last in convent

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of demons are rearranged
last in picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The final demons ruined the last nun in the convent.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest towards the end, the very last in a row.

clue.text: Description of planet denied to those without hope?

definitions.meaning: someone with no chance at all 'hasn't an ...'

explanation.surface: A description of a world forbidden to the hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not an earthly' is British idiom for having no chance whatever.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means belonging to our planet, and in the idiom 'not an earthly' it stands for a chance.

clue.text: Chaps following broadcasting head in project show discrimination

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for project

parts.note: to jut is to project, stick out

indicators.note: following puts the chaps after the broadcasting head

parts.note: DG is the Director-General, head of the BBC
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Men working behind a broadcasting chief show discrimination in a project.
explanation.walkthrough: The Director-General runs the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination in the sense of discernment, the ability to make sound judgments.

clue.text: Dreadful allocation of role's overlooked when working in theatre

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: casting is the allocation of parts to actors
acting as someone means taking their role, so as stands for role

explanation.surface: A dreadful piece of casting goes unnoticed in a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing a play is a job in theatre, guiding actors and staging.

clue.text: A sudden movement beside stone still

indicators.note: beside places the stone abbreviation next to the rest

parts.note: ST abbreviates stone, the unit of weight
a tic is a sudden involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A sudden jerk next to a stone that was otherwise motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, motionless.

clue.text: Man with weapon left limb twisted amidst crude flailing

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of the other letters
flailing means thrashing wildly, so the letters of crude are rearranged
twisted means turned round, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: An armed man's left leg twisted in some crude thrashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' gives GELL; 'flailing' gives CUDER, and 'amidst' puts GELL after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgeller is one who beats people with a cudgel, a short heavy club.

clue.text: Pleasant activities done without working illumination

indicators.note: without means minus, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
lights provide illumination

explanation.surface: Jobs done without electric light can still be pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ON from DONE, leaving DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delights are things that give great pleasure, enjoyable pursuits.

clue.text: Start to get keen after trimming lawn etc.

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word that follows
trimming means cutting off the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: ardent means keen, eager

explanation.surface: Instructions to get eager about mowing the lawn and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden includes a lawn, flowerbeds and other planted areas, hence etc.

clue.text: Sensitive to price fluctuations, business centre curtailed transaction after reflection

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the combined pieces are read backwards
curtailed means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
a sale is a transaction

explanation.surface: An economist's view of a shortened deal in the City, looked at in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial centre. 'curtailed' cuts CITY to CIT; CIT + SALE read backwards gives ELASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: In economics, elastic demand is demand that changes greatly when prices change.

clue.text: Celebrated Judge, getting over reserve, imprisoning Communist? On the contrary

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, one piece enclosing another
on the contrary reverses which piece imprisons which

parts.note: Red is a common label for a Communist
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ice means coldness of manner, reserve

explanation.surface: A judge who has overcome his reserve celebrates jailing a Communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the surface: RED actually holds J, O, ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejoiced means showed great joy, the past tense of celebrate.

clue.text: Like many deliveries, finished with a lot of force

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, dropping the last letter

parts.note: an army is a military force

explanation.surface: Hard work finished with lots of force, like many heavy deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowlers deliver the ball overarm, with the arm above the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowling, a delivery, is normally made with the arm swung above shoulder height.

clue.text: Hardy location to an extent filling southern area

indicators.note: filling means going inside

parts.note: in part means to an extent

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy setting partly takes up a southern area of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy suggests the novelist, but it means tough: the Spartans were famed for hardiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was home to famously tough, austere warriors.

clue.text: Artist showing tea in heap

indicators.note: in places the tea inside the heap

parts.note: a dump is a heap, a mess
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: An artist exhibits a cup of tea sitting in a heap of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Duchamp was a French artist, famous for readymades such as the urinal Fountain.

clue.text: The last thing to appear in parade at Hartlepool

indicators.note: to appear in says the letters show up within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The final item to feature in a parade at the town of Hartlepool.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartlepool is a port town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying is the end of life, the final event anyone experiences.

clue.text: Get rid of opponent importing large quantity of stuff from Greenland?

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for killing them, getting rid of them

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the large abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a foe is an opponent

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a rival who imports a lot of goods from Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of floating frozen sea water, plentiful around Greenland's coast.

clue.text: Desires start to surface later in loose women

indicators.note: to surface later means coming up further on, so the opening letter moves along

parts.note: sluts is a derogatory term for promiscuous women
the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Desires begin to show up later among promiscuous women.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusts are strong desires, especially sexual ones.

clue.text: Pragmatic fellow's put off about celebrity

indicators.note: put off here means taken away or discarded, so these two letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a realist is a pragmatic person
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A practical man is put off by a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The top tier of celebrities; as a modifier it means of celebrity status.

clue.text: Judges taken on board by substantial practice

indicators.note: taken on board means taken inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: real means substantial, actually existing
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: Judges taking on board a substantial body of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance.

clue.text: Students on drugs, apparently from public schools?

indicators.note: on means after, putting the drugs piece first

parts.note: high means intoxicated by drugs
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: Pupils on drugs, it seems, are from expensive schools.
explanation.walkthrough: British public schools are actually exclusive fee-paying schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Fee-paying British public schools are associated with an upper-class background.

clue.text: Man wanting no time near fellow

indicators.note: wanting no means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man without any time for the fellow next to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' is not about position: it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is old slang for stingy, so a near fellow is a hoarder of money.
